---
title: "simstim forward"
---

<!-- Generated by `just docs` from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Forward chosen session ports, or one laptop port in reverse.

```text
simstim forward <host>/<session> [<port>…] [flags]
```

Forwards the named session ports to 127.0.0.1 on this machine until Ctrl+C. Write local:guest to choose another local port. A sandbox forward grants that exact guest port and uses a private Unix socket on the host. With no port, a sandbox lists its claimed ports and asks. Use `--reverse` laptop[:guest] to reach one laptop loopback service from a sandbox on an own host. SSH forwards refuse RemoteForward, Tunnel and ForkAfterAuthentication yes in the host's SSH config.

## Examples

```sh
simstim forward my-vps/auth-fix 3000
simstim forward my-vps/auth-fix 8080:3000
simstim forward my-vps/auth-fix --reverse 5432
```

## Flags

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--reverse <string>` | Make one laptop port[:guest port] available inside an own-host sandbox |

## Flags from the parent command

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--debug[=<categories>]` | turn on the debug mode, with every category, or with the categories listed: attach, net, memory, launcher, runtime. A list binds only in the = form, such as `--debug=net` |
| `--debug-file <file>` | write the client's debug records to this file. On its own, it turns on every category (SIMSTIM_DEBUG_FILE does the same) |
| `--no-color` | print no colour (NO_COLOR does the same) |
| `--no-input` | ask nothing: a question that needs an answer fails with exit code 4, and names the flag that answers it (SIMSTIM_NO_INPUT=1 does the same) |
